page.layout: One page of text. Running head at the top across the page. Left: two woodcut illustrations of yoked oxen, stacked, occupying the left upper area. Right of the illustrations: one text column of running text, continuing below the illustrations at full width. Below that: a large woodcut of two men carrying crosses, at full width, with the catchword-like word "Subij-" at the lower right.

main_text.p: tiquis curribus tale reperio, qui sunt in Columnâ Traiani aut Antonini. Vide imagines. Dixeris hoc non falsò iugum sustinere aut sufferre, quà collo supero boum impositum est, & iugũ illi adnexum. Sed & ipsum temonẽ: (nam lectio Græca variat, vt dixi) hoc ipso, quòd ita in collo firmum, temonem attollit & prohibet à casu aut delapsu. An & ad Dionysij descriptionem aptari potest? potest dupliciter. Siue vt à pectore stipes longior & ipse temo propendeat: siue potius vt à tergo, quod res magis poscit. In figuris vide & cogita.

page.notes: Two woodcuts of yoked oxen (upper and lower) and one woodcut of two men carrying crosses on the lower part of the page; illustrations are not transcribed. Catchword "Subij-" is read from the lower right. Possible misprints not confirmed.
